text:
Yes. A commit's hash covers its parent hash, tree, author/committer info, and message. Rebase replays commits onto a new base, so each one gets a new parent, which changes its hash, and that change cascades to every descendant commit.

Exceptions: commits that end up with an identical parent, tree, and metadata keep their hashes. This happens when a rebase is a no-op, or when a fast-forward leaves the leading commits unchanged. Rewording, squashing, or editing a commit also changes its hash.

This is why rebasing commits you've already pushed requires a force-push and can disrupt collaborators.
